requirements.title: The export document
requirements.rationale: The owner can take the whole library out at any moment, in one file a program can read.

criteria.action: return one JSON document holding the user's email and display name, every link of the user, every workspace, every topic and every tag, ending with the member "complete": true, as a file download
criteria.contract: HTTP 200, Content-Type application/json, Content-Disposition 'attachment; filename="alexandria-export-<YYYY-MM-DD>.json"' dated by the request time; body {format: 'alexandria-export', version: 1, exported_at, user: {email, name}, links: [...], workspaces: [...], topics: [...], tags: [...], complete: true} with complete as the last member

setup: a user with 3 links, 2 workspaces, 2 topics and 4 tags seeded through each package's store
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts: setNow(2026-11-07T10:00Z); r = api('GET', '/api/v1/export'); assert r.status == 200 and the content type and the filename 'alexandria-export-2026-11-07.json'; body = r.json; assert body.format == 'alexandria-export' and version == 1 and user == {email, name}; assert counts 3, 2, 2, 4; assert the raw text ends with '"complete":true}'

criteria.action: for any link of the user, in any state, give it exactly one export entry equal to the body GET /api/v1/links/{id} returns for it, plus snapshot_url and reader_url, absolute on PUBLIC_ORIGIN, pointing at the export snapshot and reader routes, or null when nothing of that kind is stored

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts, a table over links {pending; active with snapshot and reader view; active PDF; 'not a web page' with no snapshot; unreachable; dormant; archived; dead; pinned; with manually edited title and tags; with a note; in two workspaces; used 7 times}: e = export.links.find(id); assert omit(e, ['snapshot_url', 'reader_url']) == api('GET', '/api/v1/links/' + id).json; assert e.snapshot_url == PUBLIC_ORIGIN + '/api/v1/export/links/' + id + '/snapshot' when a snapshot is stored, else null, and likewise reader_url; assert export.links.length == the number of links

criteria.action: give each of the user's workspaces its id, name, description, note and the ids of its links in manual order, and each of the user's topics and tags its id, name and link count
criteria.contract: workspaces: [{id, name, description, note, link_ids}]; topics: [{id, name, link_count}]; tags: [{id, name, link_count}]; a workspace's link_ids equal the order GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id} lists

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts: seed workspace 'Research' with links [b, a] in that order and a note, topic 'databases' on 2 links, tag 'sql' on 3; assert export.workspaces[0] == {id, name: 'Research', description, note, link_ids: [b, a]}; assert the topic's link_count == 2 and the tag's == 3

criteria.action: for any export, include no part of the stored AI provider key, no personal access token secret or hash, no session identifier or hash, no import report, and no data of any other user

setup: user A with an AI key 'sk-ant-test-abcd1234', two tokens, a session and a finished import; user B with links, workspaces, topics and tags of its own
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts: text = raw body of A's export; assert text contains neither 'sk-ant-test-abcd1234', '1234' as the key's last four, the encrypted key value, any token secret or secret_hash, nor any session id or hash; assert no id, URL, name or note of B appears

criteria.action: complete the export of a library of 20,000 links, each with tags, a topic and workspace membership, in under 60 seconds, sending the document as it is read rather than after it is built

setup: a user with 20,000 links, 500 tags, 100 topics and 50 workspaces seeded directly through the stores into local D1
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts: t0 = performance.now(); r = SELF.fetch('/api/v1/export', bearer); assert the first chunk of the body arrives before the last link is read (the response is streamed); body = await r.json(); assert performance.now() - t0 < 60000; assert body.links.length == 20000 and body.complete == true

criteria.condition: reading the library fails part-way through an export that has already started
criteria.action: abort the response stream, so that the download ends with an error and never contains the closing "complete": true
criteria.contract: the response body stream errors before its end; the received text does not contain '"complete":true' and does not parse as JSON

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts: seed 300 links; make the link store's page read throw on its third page; r = api('GET', '/api/v1/export'); read the body; assert reading rejects; assert the received text lacks '"complete":true' and JSON.parse(text) throws

requirements.title: Fetching stored content from the export
requirements.rationale: A backup is only complete if the stored pages can be retrieved with it, and retrieving them must not count as using them.

criteria.condition: an authenticated user requests GET /api/v1/export/links/{id}/snapshot for one of their links, in any state including archived, that has a stored snapshot
criteria.action: serve the stored snapshot exactly as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/snapshot serves it, recording no use
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the same status, Content-Type, Content-Security-Policy and body bytes as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/snapshot (text/html or application/pdf); the link's use_count and last_used_at are unchanged and no use event is added

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts, a table over {an HTML link; a PDF link; an archived HTML link}: a = api('GET', '/api/v1/export/links/' + id + '/snapshot', {bearer}); assert a.status == 200; assert use_count unchanged and no new use event; then b = api('GET', '/api/v1/links/' + id + '/snapshot'); assert a's content type, CSP header and bytes equal b's

criteria.condition: an authenticated user requests GET /api/v1/export/links/{id}/reader for one of their links, in any state including archived, that has a stored reader view
criteria.action: serve the stored reader view exactly as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader serves it, recording no use
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the same Content-Type and body as GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader; the link's use_count and last_used_at are unchanged and no use event is added

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts, a table over {an HTML link; a PDF link; an archived link}: a = export reader; assert 200 and use_count unchanged; assert a's content type and body equal those of GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader

criteria.condition: an export snapshot or reader request names a link that has nothing of that kind stored, a link of another user, or no link
criteria.action: serve nothing and record no use
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with body {"error": "no_content"} for the user's own link with nothing stored, and {"error": "not_found"} for another user's link or an unknown id, the two latter identical

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts, a table over {own pending link: no_content; own 'not a web page' link: no_content; another user's link with a snapshot: not_found; random id: not_found} crossed with {snapshot, reader}: assert status 404 and the error; assert no use_count changed

requirements.title: Exporting from the website
requirements.rationale: Taking the library out is one click on the settings page.

criteria.condition: the owner opens the settings page
criteria.action: offer an 'Export library' action that downloads GET /api/v1/export as a file
criteria.contract: the settings page has a link labelled 'Export library' with href /api/v1/export and the download attribute

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx: renderPage('/settings'); assert a link named 'Export library' with href '/api/v1/export' and a download attribute

requirements.title: Requesting account deletion
requirements.rationale: Leaving must be as deliberate as typing one's own address, and take effect at once for everything that can act as the owner.

criteria.condition: a user signed in with a session requests DELETE /api/v1/me with confirm_email equal to the account's email, compared case-insensitively with surrounding whitespace ignored
criteria.action: at once delete every session and personal access token and the stored AI provider key of the user, mark the account for deletion with the request time, queue the deletion job and clear the session cookie
criteria.contract: HTTP 202 with body {"status": "deleting"} and a Set-Cookie that expires 'alexandria_session'; the user's sessions and tokens rows are gone and the AI key column is empty; one message for the user is on ACCOUNT_QUEUE

setup: a user with two sessions, three tokens, an AI key and links
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts, a table over confirm_email {'owner@example.test', '  Owner@Example.TEST '}: r = api('DELETE', '/api/v1/me', {as: session, body: {confirm_email}}); assert r.status == 202 and r.json == {status: 'deleting'} and the cookie is expired; assert 0 sessions and 0 tokens for the user, no stored AI key, deletion_requested_at == now and one ACCOUNT_QUEUE message

criteria.condition: DELETE /api/v1/me carries no confirm_email or one that differs from the account's email
criteria.action: delete nothing and keep the user signed in
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with body {"error": "confirmation_mismatch", "field": "confirm_email", "message": "type your email address to confirm"}; sessions, tokens, the AI key and every link are unchanged; no queue message

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts, a table over bodies {{}, {confirm_email: ''}, {confirm_email: 'other@example.test'}, {confirm_email: 'owner@example.tes'}}: assert 400 with the envelope; assert row counts unchanged and GET /api/v1/me with the session still answers 200

criteria.condition: DELETE /api/v1/me is authenticated by a personal access token rather than a session
criteria.action: refuse the deletion and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with body {"error": "session_required", "message": "delete the account from the settings page"}; nothing is deleted or marked

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: r = api('DELETE', '/api/v1/me', {bearer: createToken(user), body: {confirm_email: user.email}}); assert r.status == 403 and r.json.error == 'session_required'; assert the account is not marked and the token still works

criteria.condition: the email of an account marked for deletion completes a Google sign-in before the deletion job has finished
criteria.action: create no user and no session and tell the visitor the account is being deleted
criteria.contract: HTTP 302 with Location '/signin?error=deleting'; no session cookie; the sign-in page shows 'Your account is being deleted, try again in a few minutes'; after the job has finished the same email signs in to a new user with no links

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: request deletion; complete a sign-in for the same email through the fake token endpoint of src/worker/auth/auth.test.ts's setup; assert 302 to '/signin?error=deleting' and no session; run the deletion job to the end; sign in again; assert 302 to '/' and GET /api/v1/links answers {items: []}; and in src/web/pages/SignIn.test.tsx assert error=deleting shows the message

requirements.title: The deletion job
requirements.rationale: Every trace of the account must go, however large the library and whatever fails on the way, and nothing of anyone else's.

criteria.condition: the deletion job runs for an account marked for deletion
criteria.action: remove every row that belongs to the account or to one of its links from every table of the database, found from the schema, and every R2 object under the account's prefix u/{user_id}/, and remove the user record last
criteria.contract: afterwards no table has a row whose user id is the account's or whose link id is one of its former links, SNAPSHOTS lists no object under u/{user_id}/, and the users row is gone; every other user's rows and objects are unchanged

setup: user A with links in every state, uses, fetch history, HTML and PDF snapshots and reader views, summaries, topics, tags, workspaces with notes, link notes, a finished import and an AI key; user B with the same kinds of data
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: snapshotB = every row of every table (from sqlite_master) referencing B plus B's R2 listing with bodies; request A's deletion; run the ACCOUNT_QUEUE consumer until it stops re-queueing; for every table from sqlite_master with a user_id or link_id column assert no row references A or A's former link ids; assert SNAPSHOTS.list({prefix: 'u/' + A + '/'}) is empty and A's users row is gone; assert B's rows and objects equal snapshotB

criteria.action: remove a library of 20,000 links with a snapshot and a reader view each within 10 minutes of the deletion request, working in batches of at most 1,000 rows or objects and queueing the next batch until nothing remains

setup: user A with 20,000 links, each with a stored snapshot and reader view in local R2
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: t0 = performance.now(); request deletion; drive the ACCOUNT_QUEUE consumer message by message; assert no batch deletes more than 1,000 rows or objects; assert nothing of A remains and performance.now() - t0 < 600000

criteria.condition: a run of the deletion job fails part-way, from a D1 or R2 error or the Worker's time limit
criteria.action: leave what was already removed removed and let the retried run continue with what remains, restoring nothing
criteria.contract: the consumer retries the message; the next run ends with nothing of the account remaining; a run on an account already fully deleted acknowledges its message and changes nothing

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: seed 2,500 links with snapshots; make the R2 delete throw on the second batch; run the consumer; assert the message was retried and some rows are already gone; restore R2; run again until done; assert nothing remains; run the job once more for the same user; assert it acknowledges and changes nothing

criteria.condition: the 5-minute Cron Trigger fires while an account has been marked for deletion for more than 5 minutes
criteria.action: run the deletion job for that account, so that a lost or exhausted queue message cannot stop the deletion from finishing
criteria.contract: after the scheduled run and the batches it starts, nothing of the account remains; accounts marked less than 5 minutes ago are left to their queued job

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts: mark user A for deletion at now - 6 min and user C at now - 1 min with no queue messages; run the scheduled handler with cron '*/5 * * * *'; drive the queue; assert A is fully removed and C is untouched by the sweep

requirements.title: Nothing comes back after deletion
requirements.rationale: Work queued before the deletion must not write the owner's data back after the job removed it.

criteria.system: background work (fetch, enrichment, import, liveness and decay)
criteria.action: for any fetch, enrichment, import, liveness or decay work that runs for an account marked for deletion or already removed, or for a link that no longer exists, write no row and no R2 object and make no request to an origin or to an AI provider

setup: user A with a pending link, an unenriched active link, an import in progress and links due for liveness and decay; A then marked for deletion
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts, a table over {a FETCH_QUEUE message for A's pending link; an ENRICH_QUEUE message for A's unenriched link; the next import step for A's import; the daily cron's liveness and decay pass; a FETCH_QUEUE message for a link id that no longer exists}: record D1 row counts and A's R2 listing, and count outbound fetches through the test's outbound handler; run the work; assert counts and listing unchanged and no outbound request was made; assert each message is acknowledged rather than retried

requirements.title: Deleting the account from the website
requirements.rationale: The settings page is where the owner leaves, and it must make the step unmistakable.

criteria.condition: the owner types into the delete-account field on the settings page
criteria.action: keep the 'Delete account' button disabled until the typed text equals the owner's email, compared case-insensitively with surrounding whitespace ignored, and say that deletion removes every link, snapshot, workspace, token and the AI key and cannot be undone
criteria.contract: the button is disabled for any other text and enabled for the email; the warning text is visible

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx with a fake API whose /api/v1/me is owner@example.test: a table over typed text {'', 'owner@example.tes', ' OWNER@example.test '}: assert the button is disabled, disabled, enabled; assert the warning mentions that it cannot be undone

criteria.condition: the owner presses the enabled 'Delete account' button
criteria.action: send DELETE /api/v1/me with the typed email and, when it answers 202, go to the sign-in page, which says the account and all its data are being deleted
criteria.contract: one DELETE /api/v1/me with {confirm_email: <typed text>}; the browser is at /signin?deleted=1 showing 'Your account and all its data are being deleted.'

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx: type the email, press the button; assert one DELETE /api/v1/me with the body; assert navigation to '/signin?deleted=1'; in src/web/pages/SignIn.test.tsx assert deleted=1 shows 'Your account and all its data are being deleted.'

criteria.condition: DELETE /api/v1/me fails or answers with a status other than 202
criteria.action: stay on the settings page with the owner signed in and show why the deletion did not happen
criteria.contract: the page still shows the settings; the API's message is shown, or 'could not delete the account, try again' when the request failed without one

check.pseudocode: in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx, a table over the fake API's answers {400 confirmation_mismatch with its message; network error; 500}: press the button; assert no navigation and the expected message

execution_paths.title: The owner exports the library and a script fetches a stored snapshot from it

steps.action: chooses 'Export library' on the settings page
streams the document with every link, workspace, topic and tag, ending with "complete": true
reads the file and requests one link's snapshot_url with 'Authorization: Bearer <secret>'
serves the stored snapshot without recording a use
opens the link's detail page and sees its use count unchanged

setup: wrangler dev with local D1, R2 and Queues; the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts
the owner has added two pages served by e2e/fake-origin.ts, fetched by the fetch worker, created a workspace holding one of them and a personal access token
end_state: the downloaded file parses as JSON with two links, one workspace and complete: true
the script's request to the first link's snapshot_url answered 200 with the HTML that e2e/fake-origin.ts served
the link's use_count is the same before and after the script's request
smoke.pseudocode: in e2e/export.spec.ts: sign in, add the two fake-origin pages, wait until they are no longer pending, create a workspace and a token; on /settings click 'Export library' and await the download; doc = JSON.parse(file); expect doc.links.length == 2 and doc.complete; before = doc.links[0].use_count; r = request.get(doc.links[0].snapshot_url, bearer); expect 200 and the fake page's HTML; expect request.get('/api/v1/links/' + id).use_count == before

execution_paths.title: The owner deletes the account and nothing of it remains

steps.action: types the account's email on the settings page and presses 'Delete account'
sends DELETE /api/v1/me with the typed email
deletes every session, token and the AI key, marks the account for deletion, queues the deletion job and clears the session cookie
shows the sign-in page saying the account and all its data are being deleted
requests GET /api/v1/links with the owner's former token and is refused with 401
removes the account's rows and its R2 objects in batches and the user record last
signs in again with Google after the deletion has finished and finds an empty stream

setup: wrangler dev with local D1, R2 and Queues; ALLOWED_EMAILS includes owner@example.test; the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts
the owner has two fetched links with snapshots served by e2e/fake-origin.ts, a workspace, a personal access token and an AI key accepted by e2e/fake-ai.ts
end_state: the browser was at /signin?deleted=1 immediately after the button was pressed
the script's request with the former token got 401 {"error": "unauthorized"}
within 10 minutes no D1 row references the former user or its links, and the local R2 bucket holds no object under its prefix
the second sign-in created a new user whose stream is empty
smoke.pseudocode: in e2e/account-deletion.spec.ts: set up the library; type the email on /settings and press 'Delete account'; expect url '/signin?deleted=1'; expect request.get('/api/v1/links', bearer).status == 401; poll `wrangler d1 execute --local` for rows referencing the old user id and the local R2 listing for the prefix until both are empty, failing after 10 minutes; sign in again; expect zero cards
